summary: Scientist specializing in LC-MS-based proteomics and data analysis. Ph.D. in Biology with 5+ years bridging large-scale cell-based molecular studies with rigorous statistical modeling (R, Python, SQL) and multi-omics integration to drive translational oncology and drug-discovery insights for cross-functional teams; fluent in Mandarin and English.

projects.name: Proteomic Drug-Perturbation Platform for Cancer Drug Resistance
projects.affiliation: Schweppe Lab at Univeristy of Washington
projects.summary: Designed and executed a large-scale proteomic drug-perturbation platform across multiple human cancer cell lines and multiple therapeutics, generating and analyzing over 1,000 reproducible proteome and viability profiles. Identified drug-induced network rewiring and protein complex remodeling linking cell signaling and stress-response pathways to resistance and adaptive drug response, and built predictive models to estimate drug sensitivity from molecular features.

projects.name: MPK4 Kinase Signaling in Plant Immunity
projects.affiliation: Sixue Chen Lab at Univeristy of Florida
projects.summary: Mapped the MPK4 kinase interactome and phosphorylation dynamics in plant guard cells using TurboID proximity labeling and phosphoproteomics, revealing molecular networks underlying stomatal immune responses in Arabidopsis. Developed and documented standardized protocols (SOPs) to improve reproducibility across experiments.

collaboration.name: Mapping Membrane Lipid–Protein Interactions
collaboration.collaborator: Zhongwu Guo Lab at Univeristy of Florida
collaboration.summary: This project used bifunctional chemical probes — a diazirine group in the lipid tail for UV-triggered photo-crosslinking, paired with a clickable alkyne on the glycan headgroup — to capture and identify membrane proteins that interact with glycosphingolipids (GSLs) and GPI-anchors. Ran LC-MS/MS to identify and quantify the crosslinked, biotin-tagged interacting proteins.

collaboration.name: Mapping de novo Designed Oligomers Downstream Signaling
collaboration.collaborator: David Baker Lab at University of Washington
collaboration.summary: This project used computationally designed cyclic protein oligomers displaying a synthetic FGFR-binding module to create tunable agonists whose valency and geometry control FGF/MAPK and calcium signaling, steering stem-cell differentiation toward either endothelial cells or pericytes during vascular development. Ran a comparative phosphoproteomics experiment via LC-MS/MS on FGFR1c-expressing CHO cells treated with the designed agonist (C6-79C_mb7) or natural FGF2, quantifying whole-proteome and phosphopeptide abundance changes to show the synthetic agonist faithfully reproduces natural FGF2 signaling.
